name: Why So High
tagline: Snap your electricity bill. Why So High tells you why it went up and what you can do about it this month.
scope: AEP Ohio residential customers in Columbus, Ohio

entry_points.http: POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/run with a request like input_examples/example_1.json (after npm run serve)
entry_points.web: npm run web:build && npm run serve

sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true is the default with no .env. The agent code runs unchanged on model and SQL responses recorded from a live run in samples/cache/. A new request with bill fields also runs: its weather join is computed from the NOAA copy in data/snapshot/ and logged as source snapshot. A bill image that was never recorded needs the live stack.

agents.name: BillReader
agents.role: Reads the bill image into structured fields with Nemotron; falls back to the bill's text layer with a Nemotron text model

agents.name: WeatherAnalyst
agents.role: Joins the household's bills with NOAA daily weather in one federated Zetaris query and fits or picks the weather model

agents.name: RateAnalyst
agents.role: Loads AEP Ohio's published tariff versions from OpenEI URDB through Zetaris and recomputes the bill

agents.name: UsageAnalyst
agents.role: Splits the dollar change into price, extra days, weather, usage and unexplained

agents.name: ReconciliationCritic
agents.role: Runs checks 1 to 5 and sends work back to the analysts with the reason when a check fails

agents.name: ActionPlanner
agents.role: Proposes assistance programs and actions with amounts from the household's facts

agents.name: HouseholdMemory
agents.role: Meterless H-MEM: stores diagnoses and what the household tells us

agents.name: WorldModel
agents.role: Meterless World Model: household graph with provenance on every fact

agents.name: Orchestrator
agents.role: Runs the agents in order and routes the critic's send-backs

models.used_by: Evaluation baseline only (bill text, no tools)

agent_framework: None. The orchestrator is plain TypeScript.

sponsor_technology.zetaris: Federated SQL over the sources in place, nothing copied into the app: every run joins the household bills in Postgres with NOAA NCEI daily weather (REST) in one query (WeatherAnalyst) and reads AEP Ohio's tariff versions from OpenEI URDB (REST) (RateAnalyst). EIA retail sales (REST) is registered too; the statewide Ohio prior was fitted once from it and is a constant in src/agents/weatherAnalyst.ts, not a query per run. Registered with npm run setup:sources (src/zetaris/sources.ts, src/zetaris/queries.ts).
sponsor_technology.meterless: Nightshift is the model runtime for every model call (src/llm/nightshift.ts). H-MEM and World Model, vendored unchanged in engines/, hold the household's memory, and that memory changes the diagnosis and the action plan.
sponsor_technology.nvidia: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads the bill image, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the text layer when vision fails, and Nemotron 3 Ultra is the bill-only baseline in the evaluation. The model served is logged on every call.
sponsor_technology.cursor: Not used. The code was written with Claude Code (Anthropic). The organizers' HackOS FAQ lists Cursor as optional.

data_sources.name: NOAA NCEI daily summaries, Columbus station USW00014821
EIA retail sales API
data_sources.use: Ohio residential sales per customer, Jan 2025 to Jul 2026, fitted once into the statewide weather prior

data_sources.name: EIA RECS 2020, table CE4.3
data_sources.use: Heating slope of electric-heat homes in the evaluation generator

data_sources.name: ODJFS, PUCO and AEP Ohio program pages, read 22 Oct 2026
data_sources.use: Program amounts, income limits and dates in src/actions/programs.ts
data_sources.license: Public program information, cited per value

data_sources.name: Linda's household and bills
data_sources.license: Synthetic, generated from the published tariff by scripts/make-sample-bill.ts

pre_existing_components: Meterless H-MEM and World Model engines (Apache-2.0), vendored unchanged from github.com/Meterless/Meterless at commit 1742dec, listed in engines/VENDORED.md
